newsitem.title: UK: Treats in growth plan after profit fall.
newsitem.headline: Treats in growth plan after profit fall.

text.p: Frozen confectionery maker Treats Group Plc on Monday posted lower profits in its first full-year results since joining the UK stock market last June, but set out a growth plan intended to reduce seasonal swings in its sales.

The company said pre-tax profit fell to 1.4 million stg in the year ended December 31 from 2.4 million a year before. It blamed weather conditions which did not create sustained buying patterns and had led to higher cold storage costs.

It said heavy depreciation costs and expenditure on new machinery had also hit profits, but said it planned new products which sold more steadily year-round as well as an expansion overseas where the sun shines longer or at different times.

Treats said its "5-Ice" product launched late in 1996 had already become the UK's second biggest in its category, and said it had contracted with SmithKline Beecham Plc to develop products based on its Ribena and Lucozade brands.
"We enter the year with strong foundations, new markets and products," said chairman Brian Fidler, "and the capacity to handle substantially increased sales given the right climate."
Turnover rose slightly to 22.3 million stg from 22.2 million and Treats paid a total dividend of 3.0p per share.
